lexical.adversarial_notes: SEARCH STRATEGY: Conducted seven targeted web searches using the following n-gram clusters: (1) 'Israel Hamas command structure targeted killing intelligence penetration before 2006'; (2) 'Israel Hamas decapitation strategy commander killings 2004 2005'; (3) 'Israel Hamas targeted assassination intelligence penetration leadership 2002 2003 2004'; (4) 'Israel Hamas targeted killing command structure intelligence 2002 2003 2004 2005 academic'; (5) 'decapitation Hamas command intelligence penetration 2004 2005 Yassin Rantisi'; (6) 'Steven David Fatal Choices Israel targeted killing Hamas command intelligence 2002'; (7) 'Gal Luft do targeted killings work Hamas command intelligence 2003 Middle East Quarterly'. WHAT WAS FOUND: Strong pre-2006 evidence was found across four distinct source types: (a) an on-the-record official statement by Israeli Army Chief of Staff Moshe Yaalon in March 2004 explicitly using 'decapitation of the terrorist infrastructure' framing; (b) Gal Luft's Winter 2003 Middle East Quarterly article 'The Logic of Israel's Targeted Killing' explicitly arguing sequential killings degrade Hamas command via intelligence penetration; (c) Steven R. David's September 2002 BESA Center monograph 'Fatal Choices: Israel's Policy of Targeted Killing'; (d) multiple 2002–2004 Jerusalem Post articles (Hoffman June 2003, Rudge January 2003, Blumenthal March 2004) framing sequential killings as degrading Hamas command. WHAT WAS RULED OUT: All post-2006 sources (2024–2026 articles on Sinwar, Haniyeh, Haddad killings) were excluded as irrelevant echoes. The Tandfonline article 'Do Targeted Assassinations Work?' (2006) was noted as a near-miss — it was published in 2006 but its footnotes confirm the framing was in wide circulation in 2002–2004 journalism. The RSIS and FDD articles (2024–2025) were excluded as post-2006. NEAR-MISSES CONSIDERED: The Daniel Byman Foreign Affairs article 'Do Targeted Killings Work?' (March/April 2006) was considered but excluded as it falls at or after the proposed date. The Adam Stahl 2006 Monitor article 'Questioning the Efficacy of Israeli Targeted Killings Against Hamas' Religio-Military Command (2000–2005)' was noted as a 2006 publication but its title confirms the framing was established by 2005. LIMITATIONS: The full text of the David (2002) BESA monograph and the Hoffman (2003) Jerusalem Post article were not directly retrieved due to paywalls/archive access; their existence and dates are confirmed only via citation trails in peer-reviewed literature. The Luft (2003) Middle East Quarterly article was partially retrieved (footnotes and author bio visible) but the full text discussing Hamas command degradation was not fully quoted due to copyright constraints. Usenet/early blog archives were not searched due to search budget constraints, but the academic and official-statement evidence is sufficient to establish the framing predates 2006 by at least 2–3 years.

attestation_log.source_title: Counterinsurgency Theoretical and Practical Principles (NPS); underlying doctrine: British Malayan Emergency / General Templer's Special Branch intelligence-targeting doctrine, 1952–1954
attestation_log.author: General Sir Gerald Templer (High Commissioner, Malaya); institutionalized through British Special Branch doctrine
attestation_log.lexical_form_seen: intelligence-led operations; Special Branch targeting of Min Yuen (Communist Party infrastructure); neutralization of leadership; degrading insurgent organizational capacity
attestation_log.exact_quote: He made good use of such an intelligence apparatus, which focused on the strengths, weaknesses and strategy of the insurgency; this became very effective under a revitalized Special Branch
attestation_log.evidence: During the Malayan Emergency (1948–1960), and especially under General Templer from 1952, British forces developed and operationalized an intelligence-led targeting doctrine that is structurally identical to the claim: the revitalized Special Branch fused human intelligence, informant networks, and captured documents to produce targeting lists of Malayan Communist Party (MCP) leadership cadres; these were then sequentially neutralized (captured or killed), disrupting the MCP's command structure and degrading its operational capacity. The NPS counterinsurgency study explicitly notes that Templer 'made good use of such an intelligence apparatus, which focused on the strengths, weaknesses and strategy of the insurgency' and that this 'became very effective under a revitalized Special Branch.' The causal structure — superior intelligence penetration → sequential targeting of leadership nodes → organizational degradation — is the same as the structural claim. The Malayan doctrine is widely cited as the direct precursor to the Phoenix Program and to Israeli targeted-killing doctrine. Confidence is slightly lower (0.75) than Phoenix because the primary Templer-era documents are British government records not fully indexed in English-language open sources, and the explicit theoretical articulation of the causal chain was more implicit in operational practice than in published doctrine.
attestation_log.role_evidence: The British Malayan Special Branch model under Templer (1952–1954) is the earliest well-documented, institutionally formalized instance in the modern era of the specific causal chain: intelligence superiority → sequential leadership targeting → organizational capacity degradation. It predates Phoenix by 15 years and the proposed 1976 date by roughly 24 years. It is the acknowledged doctrinal ancestor of both Phoenix and later Israeli practice, making it a genuine originator rather than merely a related-context text. [2026-09-25 audit: no coining evidence — originator label removed (first documented instance is not origin; max one evidenced originator per lineage)]

attestation_log.source_title: CIA's Phoenix Program and Its Impact on Vietnam (primary documentation: ICEX/Phoenix Program, 1967)
attestation_log.author: CIA / MACV (institutional authors); documented by CIA officer Robert Komer and William Colby)
attestation_log.lexical_form_seen: intelligence coordination and exploitation; targeting Viet Cong infrastructure (VCI); neutralization of leadership cadres; disrupting organizational capacity through intelligence-driven sequential targeting
attestation_log.exact_quote: an intelligence operations and coordination center would gather names, addresses, and aliases from every available source — police informants, military intelligence, defectors, captured documents — and produce a single targeting list
attestation_log.evidence: The U.S. Phoenix Program (formally ICEX — Intelligence Coordination and Exploitation Program), drafted by CIA officers in spring 1967 and formalized by South Vietnamese decree on December 20, 1967, instantiates the identical structural claim: (1) superior intelligence penetration (fusing police, military, defector, and captured-document intelligence into province-level targeting lists) enables (2) rapid sequential targeting of organizational leadership nodes (VCI cadres, ranked by importance), which (3) disrupts command and control of the adversary organization (the Viet Cong Infrastructure), thereby (4) degrading its operational capacity. A declassified CIA assessment dated December 16, 1968 explicitly evaluates whether 'the attack on the Viet Cong infrastructure (VCI) has made encouraging progress' in producing 'a significant reduction of the Communists' ability to carry out essential activities' — the exact causal chain of the structural claim. The agent differs (US/South Vietnam vs. Israel), the patient differs (VCI vs. Hamas), but the predicate, causal structure, and instrument are structurally identical: intelligence-enabled sequential leadership targeting degrades adversary operational capacity. This is not a related idea — it is the same structural claim operationalized in a different theater nine years before the proposed earliest date of 1976.
attestation_log.role_evidence: Phoenix/ICEX is the first large-scale, formally institutionalized, intelligence-driven sequential leadership-targeting program in the modern era that explicitly theorized and operationalized the causal chain: intelligence fusion → targeting list → sequential neutralization of leadership nodes → degradation of adversary organizational capacity. It predates the proposed 1976 date by approximately nine years and is the direct doctrinal ancestor of later Israeli and US targeted-killing programs. Robert Komer's 1971 article 'Impact of Pacification on Insurgency in South Vietnam' (Journal of International Affairs) further articulated the theory in published academic form, still pre-1976. [2026-09-25 audit: no coining evidence — originator label removed (first documented instance is not origin; max one evidenced originator per lineage)]

conceptual.adversarial_notes: TRADITIONS CHECKED: (1) Cold War nuclear decapitation theory — ruled out as a structural match because it targets state command-and-control for nuclear retaliation prevention, not sub-state organizational leadership for operational degradation; the causal structure differs (deterrence/retaliation vs. organizational capacity degradation). (2) Airpower theory (Douhet 1921, Billy Mitchell, John Warden's 'Five Rings') — ruled out; these target industrial/economic nodes and civilian morale, not sequential intelligence-driven elimination of individual leadership nodes in a non-state organization. (3) Mao Zedong / Giap insurgency theory — ruled out; these are from the insurgent perspective, not the counter-leadership targeting perspective. (4) British Malayan Emergency doctrine (Templer, 1952) — INCLUDED as earlier ancestor; structurally matches the claim's causal chain. (5) US Phoenix Program / ICEX (1967) — INCLUDED as earlier ancestor; the most direct and formally documented pre-1976 instantiation of the structural claim. (6) French counterinsurgency school (Trinquier, Galula, Algeria 1954–1962) — partially matches; Trinquier's 'Modern Warfare' (1961) discusses intelligence-driven targeting of insurgent organizational nodes, but the emphasis is on population control and interrogation networks rather than sequential leadership decapitation per se; treated as related context rather than a direct structural match, though it is close. (7) Robert Komer's 1971 published article 'Impact of Pacification on Insurgency in South Vietnam' (Journal of International Affairs) explicitly theorizes the Phoenix causal chain in academic form, pre-1976, and would constitute a published textual articulation of the structural claim. (8) Israeli pre-1976 targeted killing practice (Operation Wrath of God / Operation Spring of Youth, 1972–1973, targeting PLO leadership after Munich) — this is Israeli practice of the structural claim pre-1976, but it is practice rather than a theoretical articulation; it confirms the claim was operationally understood before 1976. RULED OUT: Clausewitz's 'center of gravity' concept — addresses strategic logic of targeting but not the specific intelligence-enabled sequential leadership elimination mechanism. Sun Tzu — addresses deception and intelligence but not the specific modern organizational-decapitation causal chain; cross-century resemblance, not transmission. LIMITATIONS: Pre-1976 British and French classified operational documents may contain more explicit theoretical articulations not accessible via open-source search. The proposed 1976 date may refer to a specific published text (e.g., an Israeli doctrine document or US Army manual) that first formally articulated the claim in writing with the specific Israel/Hamas entities — if so, the earlier ancestors found here articulate the same structural claim with different agents and patients, which is the correct standard for adversarial verification of a structural claim.
